evidence_set: Across sources, co-use among people who use cocaine varied widely: simultaneous alcohol 24% to 98%, simultaneous cannabis 12% to 76%, concurrent alcohol 37% to 96%, concurrent cannabis 43% to 94% (ranges as stated in the text; three of them do not match the table, whose values run 23.5% to 87%, 9.3% to 76.5% and 34.9% to 96.5%; study card reporting issue).
3. Results › 3.1.1. Review of studies including PSU prevalence, 1st paragraph; Table 1, Polysubstance use rate column

Definitions differed: simultaneous use meant use at the same time or within a couple of hours, co-administration in a session, co-use at first cocaine use, using alcohol or cannabis to come down from a cocaine high, or using them together with cocaine and a prescription drug in the past 12 months (Rx study); concurrent use meant both substances within 30 days, 6 months, a year or a lifetime, both positive in one urine test, or an unstated window (one source); several rates were calculated by the authors from the articles' data.
